body:
We just discovered this is an issue for Terrain3D users. Our downstream issue has more details and pictures: https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D/issues/827

The issue specifically is: visibility ranges are ignored on MultiMeshInstance3D shadow casting when cast_shadows is set to on/shadows_only under an OmniLight3D or SpotLight3D. I would change the title to: MultiMeshInstance3D visibility ranges ignored when casting shadows under Omni/Spot lights.

Here's an MRP that easily demonstrates this issue: 
* Create a new project.
* Download any [recent build artifact](https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D/actions?query=branch%3Amain) of Terrain3D
* Add addons/terrain_3d from the zip
* Open our Demo. On the Terrain3D tab asset dock, click Meshes then select the red LODExample.
* Right click it and:
  * Change height offset to 1 or 2 so you can see its shadows. 
  * Change last_shadow_lod to 1, so we'll only compare shadows for LOD0 (sphere) and LOD1 (cube)
* Paint one instance on the ground.
* Hide the environment, and add an OmniLight

This is the MMI setup:
* LOD0 range 0-32, cast_shadows = on
* LOD1 range 32-64, cast_shadows = on

We can ignore the other LODs. When the camera is close and rendering LOD0, it should cast shadows only for LOD0. When farther it should show and cast for LOD1.

Now look at these tests:
1. Change between the Directional Light and the Omni Light. The DL properly casts only the sphere shadow, then the cube farther. The OL incorrectly casts both sphere and cube shadows.
2. Change last_shadow_lod to 0, which will disable LOD1 shadow casting. The DL and OL correctly show the sphere shadow when rendering LOD0. However when farther and LOD1 is rendered, the DL correctly disables the shadow, while the OL incorrectly continues to cast LOD0's shadow.
3. Change last_shadow_lod to 1 and shadow_impostor to 1, which will disable LOD0 shadow casting. The DL and OL correctly shows the cube shadow when rendering LOD0 or LOD1. However when the camera is pulled back to render LOD2, the DL correctly disables the shadow, while the OL continues casting on LOD1.

Actually, this isn't limited to MMIs. It's also a problem on regular MeshInstance3Ds in 4.4.1 and 4.5.1. I would further change the title to `Visibility ranges ignored when casting shadows under Omni/Spot lights`. The cube is not visible, so the shadow should not be visible: The MRP with Terrain3D above is good for testing MMIs. But for regular meshes, just make two MeshInstance3Ds: a sphere visibility range 0-32, a cube visible 32-64, and add an omnilight with shadows enabled.
